question: How does light affect the sleep cycle in space?

response.science: Light exposure in space can disrupt circadian rhythms because astronauts experience many sunrises and sunsets per day, leading to sleep‑wake cycle disturbances. [S1] Exposure to light at inappropriate times causes circadian misalignment and sleep disruption, so mission design recommends dedicated quiet sleep quarters and controlled lighting. [S2] Countermeasures such as using LEDs to simulate Earth’s light‑dark cycle help align biological clocks. [S1] Covering windows with blinds and wearing eye masks also mitigate circadian desynchrony.
